back: The unit of amount of substance: one mole contains $6.02 \times 10^{23}$ particles (atoms, molecules or ions).

front: State the value of the **Avogadro constant**.

back: The mass of one mole of a substance, in g/mol. It has the same number as the Ar or Mr.

front: Formula linking amount, mass and molar mass
How do you find the number of particles from the amount?
How many atoms are in 1 mol of $\ce{O2}$?
How many moles of ions are in 1 mol of $\ce{CaCl2}$?
back: 3 mol: 1 mol of $\ce{Ca^2+}$ and 2 mol of $\ce{Cl-}$.

front: What must you do with a mass in kg before using amount = mass ÷ molar mass?
back: Convert it to grams (× 1000), because molar mass is in g/mol.

front: Why do 12 g of carbon and 24 g of magnesium contain the same number of atoms?
back: A magnesium atom is twice as heavy as a carbon atom (Ar 24 v 12), so twice the mass holds the same number of atoms: one mole of each.

front: Describe the 'mole map' from mass to number of particles.
back: mass $\div$ molar mass $=$ amount; amount $\times 6.02 \times 10^{23} =$ number of particles. Reverse the operations to go back.
